heroHeadline: Scribe STX-1150 Clears First-in-Human Regulatory Barrier; Editas EDIT-401 NHP: ≥90% LDL-C/Lp(a)/ApoB in Single Dose; $319M Editas Offering; CRISPR Cardiovascular Pipeline Accelerates
heroSubtitle: May 21, 2026: Scribe Therapeutics received regulatory clearance to initiate the first-in-human study of STX-1150, the world's first CRISPR epigenetic silencer (non-cutting ELXR platform, PCSK9 target) to reach clinical stage for cardiovascular disease. Simultaneous late-breaking NHP data was presented at the EAS Congress in Athens (May 24–27). May 25–26, 2026: Editas Medicine presented EDIT-401 base-editing data at the 94th EAS Congress showing a single LNP dose achieves ≥90% mean reductions in LDL-C, Lp(a), and ApoB simultaneously in non-human primates — a cardiovascular triple-target milestone — alongside positive pre-IND feedback from the FDA. On May 26, Editas priced an up to $319.4 million public offering to fund first-in-human EDIT-401 studies planned for H2 2026. May 28, 2026: CRISPR Therapeutics, Prime Medicine, and Caribou Biosciences announced June investor conferences, highlighting the full breadth of the clinical CRISPR pipeline from approved (Casgevy, 500+ patients) to prime editing's first regulatory filings (PM577 Wilson disease, H1 2026).
footerNote: Data sourced from FDA, EMA, MHRA, NIH, peer-reviewed journals (Nature, Science, NEJM, Cell), ClinicalTrials.gov, and major science outlets. Clinical data reflects published peer-reviewed results only.
